name: Mozambique
snapshot: Frelimo, in power since independence in 1975, kept the presidency after a disputed 2024 election and months of deadly protests, while an insurgency simmers in the gas-rich north.
culture: Mozambique's long coastline was part of the Swahili world before Portugal colonised it, and Island of Mozambique, the old colonial capital, is UNESCO-listed. Marrabenta music came out of Maputo's suburbs, and the timbila xylophone orchestras of the Chopi people are on UNESCO's heritage list. Mia Couto is among Africa's most celebrated novelists.
society: A civil war from 1977 to 1992 killed around a million people. Huge offshore gas finds in Cabo Delgado drew TotalEnergies and ExxonMobil, but an Islamic State-linked insurgency since 2017 has displaced over a million people. A "hidden debts" scandal in 2016 tipped the country into crisis. Most people are poor farmers.
baseline: Daniel Chapo of Frelimo was declared winner of the October 2024 election; challenger Venâncio Mondlane called it fraud and led months of protests in which hundreds were killed, the worst unrest since the civil war. Chapo took office in January 2025 and later signed a political accord with opposition parties. Rwandan troops help fight the northern insurgency.
